blocks.text: Known For: Strong naval power, magnificent temple architecture (Dravidian style), and an efficient local self -administrative system.
Most Powerful ruler: Rajendra Chola.
Vijayalaya Chola (850 AD - 871 AD)
+ He captured Thanjavur (Tanjore) from the Muttaraiyars (chiefs of the Kaveri delta) and this marked the firm establishment of Chola rule in South India.
He built a temple dedicated to goddess Nishumbhasudini (a form of Durga) at Thanjavur.
Title: Narkesari (Lion among men).
Defeated the Pallavas king Aparajita, which marked the decline of Pallava power and rise of Cholas.
+ Extended Chola influence in the Kaveri Valley.
After conquering the Madurai and Tirunelveli (Pandya Mandalam) regions, he assumed the title "Maduraikonda"
Prantaka I (907 AD-955 AD)
He lost to Rashtrakuta king Krishna III (in the Battle of Takkolam) who made a Victory Pillar and Krishneshwara temple at Rameshwaram.
The Uttaramerur inscription mentions Parantaka I.
He defeated Pandyas at Vellore and temporarily occupied Sri Lanka.
Assumed the title: "Maduraiyum Elamum Konda"
(Conqueror of Madurai and Lanka).
Issued coins called: Kasu (small denomination) and Kalanju (gold coin).
Raja Raja I (985 AD-1014AD)
He was the real founder of Chola imperialism.
He defeated Cheras at Trivandrum and conquered Madurai from Pandyas.
He conquered Maldives and invaded Sri Lanka.
Permitted the Shailendra king (from Srivijaya dynasty, Southeast Asia) to construct a Buddhist temple Monastery at Nagapattinam called Chudamani Vihara (Symbol of diplomatic and religious tolerance).
Introduced a land revenue system, organized departments like PWD.
Rajendra I (1014 AD-1044 AD)
He was the son of Raja Raja I.
He is also known as Mahmud of Ghazanavi was "Napoleon of South India". a contemporary of Rajaraja I
Launched naval expeditions #4 Rajendra I.
to Sri Lanka, Burma, the Andaman Islands, and Srivijaya (Southeast Asia).
He completely conquered Sri Lankan (Ceylon) capital Anuradhapura.
He crossed Ganga and defeated two local Kings of Bengal and took the title "Gangaikondachola" and built the city Gangaikondacholapuram as the new capital.
He built Chola Gangam Lake (Ponneri lake), situated within the vicinity of Gangaikonda Cholapuram to celebrate his northern campaign.
+ Sent an army to Ganga, brought Ganga water ina golden pot.
Conquered Andhra, Odisha, and Bengal and took the chola empire to its peak.
Rajadhiraja I > Rajendra II > Virarajendra
Continued imperial dominance.
Faced resistance from Western Chalukyas and Pandya Kulottunga I
United Chola and Eastern Chalukya lineages.
Focused more on administration and consolidation rather than aggressive expansion.
Promoted trade with Southeast Asia and China Later Cholas (Kulottunga II - Rajendra III)
Gradual decline of power.
Chola fought against the Western Chalukyas (Kalyani).
The final blow came with defeat by Pandyas in the 13th century.
Aftermath:
+ Later Cholas were replaced by Pandyas and Hoysalas in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka.
+ Later Chalukyas were replaced by Yadavas (Devagiri) and Kakatiyas (Warangal) in the Deccan.
Shailendra Dynasty was mune which believed in Buddhism Chola Territory Administration
The king of Chola Dynasty has all the authority.
He had Council of Ministers to advice him.
Chola Empire was divided into: Mandalams (province) which was further divided into Valandu (districts) — Nadus (sub-districts) + Kurram (group of villages) — Ur (village).
Cholas are known for local (decentralised)/village government.
Uttaramerur inscriptions describe a well-organized village administration.
Every village was divided into 30 yards (kudumbus).
Each yard was governed by a local committee called "Variyam"
There were two assemblies:
au Assembly of common people.
Sabha: Assembly of learned Brahmins (Agrahars:
The village assembly (Sabha) functioned through specialized committees:
Eri Variyam —> Tank & irrigation management.
Pon Variyam — Gold & finance.
Nyaya Variyam — Justice.
Members of committees were selected through the Kudavolai system (lottery method), famously described in the Uttaramerur inscriptions (Chingleput, Tamil Nadu).
People with property or land were privileged to take part in elections.
Every member of the committee was appointed for 3 years.
Famous for star- shaped temple.
